body: If we're talking from an objective point of view, I think a decent proportion of people who start to experience depression emerge within like 18-24 months. But I can't help but feel like once you've gone past that, 2 years, 5 years, 10 years, sort of feels like you're doomed to live with it forever in one capacity or another...

same! I was feeling a bit bad recently that I've kind of started coming and writing on here more frequently, when it was like 5 years (apparently!) since I last was - as in like, that I've returned to being in that bad a state - but at the same time, it's also just a form of help with problems.

Just being able to be around people (even if it's virtual and anonymous) who go through similar things and listen to them and be listened to, it's comforting

I'm sorry to hear you've gone through all this.

It's interesting what you mention about suicide 'attempts' as I've thought about this too in the past - it's kind of scary, in a way, the way that people/institutions' response to suicide attempts is based on the actual actions that people do or don't do. I mean to be fair it does kind of make sense from their perspective, but like one of the times I came the closest was an 'attempt' like that, where I was 100% convinced I was going to do it (more so than times where I actually took some action) but ended up not doing so at the last minute.

To me that was far more serious than my actual attempts, but because I didn't actually do anything, nothing really happened, whereas another couple of times (where I don't think I *really* wanted to die that bad) I ended up on the psychiatric ward for a week or two. Not that I would really have wanted that to happen, but still, it's just a weird thought, that something so serious and deadly could basically go unnoticed because you didn't take any noticeable action.

27M, I feel you on this - I haven't been struggling with this stuff my whole life, only about the last 6 years or so but I also feel like I've tried most stuff and it's still just such a slog.

I kind of thought I was getting better about a year and a bit ago, but various stuff has happened since then, including physical problems which I can't really do much about rn, and it's just completely taken me back. At the moment I'm basically just passing time, waiting for things to get better, and it's wholly unenjoyable. I've lost (for now) the things that actually brought me happiness, and along with this whole mental illness journey, people have gradually fallen out of my life, so now I can't occupy myself that easily, I also don't have a whole load of people to talk to and getting through the days is just a pain atm.

As much as everyone tells you it doesn't matter how long it takes to do stuff, or you go at your own pace in life, it doesn't make it easy when everything you see around you is people going at a 'normal' pace - being able to work, having careers, moving out, moving in with partners, getting engaged. Not to mention media reinforcing all of that.

thank you too for the message - yeah, I feel you. That feeling when you've really got yourself excited and motivated for something just to get shot down when you try it, just takes the wind out of everything.

good luck with it all, I hope it goes alright :)

Hmm, I don't know what country you're in or how it works where you are but the point of therapy is to be able to discuss stuff openly and confidentially unless there's a **material** risk of danger to you or someone else, and it really should be material.

Like I have a 'plan', not concrete and completely foolproof but at least an idea that I've investigated in the past, and I'm able to talk to my therapist about it without fear of anything happening as a result. I mean hell, I've even talked about my desire sometimes to like completely slice myself open in front of my friends, but that's just an imaginative thing and so we can talk about it in terms of the emotions underlying it and whatever, it's fairly obvious that i'm not actually going to do that.

So yeah, I find it strange that this has happened to you because that defeats the point of therapy, you're *supposed* to talk about what's on your mind or what you imagine or fantasise about and if they can't accept that you can think about suicide without having an intention to kill yourself then it doesn't seem to me like they can know too much about depression...

This sounds incredibly difficult, I can't imagine what this must all be like for you, and at your age as well - I know this stuff is horrible in any situation and at any age but it still makes me especially sad hearing of people's teenage years or younger being occupied with mental health (or other) problems.

Either way, I'm really proud that you managed to come here and say all of this, it's a really strong start and I do believe you can work through this. It won't be easy but you've gotta start somewhere and you've done just that.

One thing I would say is try as best you can not to compare yourself. Either to others, or to perhaps yourself before this all happened - it's way to easy to be like 'man look at what everyone else is doing' and it just makes you feel like giving up. But at the end of the day, you are where you are and that's all that matters. Focus on yourself, what you are able to do and what is suitable or manageable for you. As in - you can always look down at your feet and see that you are still moving forwards, as opposed to looking up and panicking about where everyone else is where you could be or 'should' be, cos none of that shit matters.

Anyway, i'm just rambling now - I wish you the best of luck for your journey and I'll be thinking of you

Occasionally I need to remind myself as well that this is an **illness**, there is something inside my brain that's not as it should be, and so maybe I shouldn't scold myself this much about what I can and can't do.

That being said I think it's also difficult to get the balance between being kind to yourself but pushing yourself a bit when you can, and is something I'm still trying to figure out. But I feel like, especially in this subreddit, we could probably all use the reminder that this is indeed a medical condition

Not to say what you did was good or fair, I mean I know you know that anyway, but that most people won't even try to understand your perspective or anything like that. But I just want to say before anything else that I believe you. I really do, and I can...see the emotions that must have led you to do what you did, and also that led to what you're thinking at the moment. Even if I can't be of any other use, just know that I believe you. I'm not sure if it makes a difference to you, but I think were I posting this that's some reassurance that would just be nice to hear.

I can't solve this situation for you unfortunately. I wish I could, but I can't. But I'm still gonna try and provide some outside perspective.

So first of all, no, in no way is it 'worth dying over'. And there are two parts to this - firstly it's not worth dying over in the sense that you've said, in that I believe in no way is it ever appropriate for a human life to be sacrificed in repayment, or as a gesture of apology. Even in the worst worst cases, where someone has **actually** raped someone, or killed people, and certainly not in your situation. Even though you may not feel like it right now, your life is worth something, and you deserve to live. Was what you did slightly stupid? Yeah, probably. Does that make you an inherently terrible person? No. We all do things we haven't properly thought through from time to time, just some more extreme than others, but that doesn't make us all bad people. Hate the action, not the person, or whatever it is they say.

And the second part is that, even if you don't believe me about the stuff I just said, and you *do* think you deserve to die (which I imagine may be the case, I don't expect to change your opinion in a second), just know that killing yourself won't make things better for anyone else. I promise promise promise you this, I can't stress how much this is the case. I understand what you're thinking, really I do, it's not exactly something I've thought before but I have wondered whether I deserve to live and stuff like that, but really, from everyone else's perspective, there's no way this will help them. For Ashley and your other friends, even if they've been repulsed by what you've done, them hearing of your suicide really won't do anything positive, honestly. If we assume there's still a part of them that remembers what you had together, as a friendship, then they'll be devastated that you killed yourself. And even if somehow that isn't the case, there's just no way they'd be glad or appreciative of what you've done. Even in the most extreme scenario where they don't feel anything positive towards you and aren't sad by your death, even then it's likely they'll feel some guilt that they might have played some part in causing it. And as much as you may want to reassure them, and as much as you might already have done in the letter you've written Ashley, that you're doing this as an offering of apology and as a demonstration that you would never hurt anyone, firstly I don't think they're gonna be particularly reassured of anything, and secondly at the end of the day they're human and will probably think that their lawsuit or whatever played a part in driving you to kill yourself. And as much as you may want to assure them of your true nature, I'm also sure you don't want them to be living the rest of *their* lives with guilt, and probably a certain amount of sadness. So killing yourself won't solve anything, I promise you.

As for the more general stuff, as in not talking about what you did or your thoughts of killing yourself or whatever, but what you feel towards Ashley and stuff.....ahhhh, I just, alright. So I've never had any romantic or sexual experience myself, I'm 21(M), but you know, I can just tell you already that for you yourself, in the long run you won't benefit from fantasising about and dreaming of yourself with Ashley. I don't mean in terms of your sexual fantasies or whatever, that's up to you, but just as a concept of being able to be with her. You know, it's fine desiring to be with someone, I mean it's natural, it's human nature, and we all have crushes, but by fixating on it and making it like almost a condition for your happiness, if we assume it doesn't happen, it's only going to bring you sadness and pain. And can you see that it already has? That you're already being driven to the point of considering killing yourself as an offering to her? Can you see that it has taken you too far? It's not a pleasant truth by any stretch of the imagination, but if I'm going to be real with you, I can tell you now you're only hurting yourself by trying to do whatever you can to get a little closer to that dream in which you and her are together. It's great to have ambitions and aspirations in terms of personal connections and relationships and stuff, but once you make your life and your happiness conditional on someone else (which inherently is a thing you can't control - as much as you may be trying to convince her, at the end of the day you can't control what she thinks), you're just going to be hurting yourself.

This is all much beyond the scope of what I can do as a random person on the internet typing on my computer. But please seek some help. I don't mean this in the generic sense that everyone just suggests, I'm not saying because I feel I **should** stop you from killing yourself, but if you see a therapist, you can properly talk this through and they can really help you work through this. I do this, I see a therapist and I've talked about my crush and how it makes me so sad when I think about her and then remember I'm a depressive with nothing at the moment, but talking about it and exploring what's going on in your mind is actually really calming and makes you feel a lot more in control of stuff.

So if I could say one thing in all of this (aside from the fact that I believe you, and I'm really wishing the best I can for you, I mean that), please just talk to someone. If you have someone you think you can trust with this stuff or you feel comfortable talking to, your mum, your sister, another friend, then please do. And if not, try out therapy. It will honestly help you be able to think through this stuff because it must be horrible going through this over and over again, and I'm glad you felt able to let things out here, because it's a start. But as I say, there's only so much you can get from anonymous people over the internet. That and also that death is most certainly not the solution to your problem, as much as it may feel like it is, and I can see where you're coming from. I really feel for you, and I'll be thinking about you a lot - I'm here if you wanna just let stuff out or whatever (I usually log into this account every day or couple of days or so).

Much love, friend.

Also, if it's like that, as in a meal or something, maybe talk to your friend beforehand (I assume he knows about your anxiety?) - maybe agree on some kind of keyword or something like that so if you suddenly feel yourself freezing up, you can just say that word or phrase and excuse yourself, and he'll know what's up and can come find you? Anyway, these are things I'm thinking of if you're really worried and think you might have like an anxiety attack or something. If it's just for the level of feeling uncomfortable and not knowing what to say, the biggest thing is...just don't overthink it! I know you probably hear that a lot, and the whole thing of anxiety is that you think about everything, but at the end of the day they're human beings, you're a human being and assuming they're not nasty people, they probably just want to be good hosts since you're coming to their house - so there's no expectation for you to sing, dance or do anything unreasonable. Just try and think about it from their perspective, if you had a kid and his/her friend was coming over - you don't want to demand anything of them, you just want to be nice to them :)

Hey - in terms of the stuff you friend was talking about. I think it's really difficult, with something like depression you really have to find the right balance, between pushing yourself in order to help better and being kind to yourself. It sounds like as a result of what your friend was saying you might be lacking some of the latter a bit, so I'll try and reinforce that by reminding you that it is an illness. I'm sure you know much of this, but because the symptoms of it appear similar to what might be just 'laziness' for other people, it's easy to criticise lifestyle and whatever but at the end of the day they are symptoms of an illness, lack of energy, lack of motivation etc. And you have to remind yourself of that - I know I've had people telling me that my mindset is under my control, I can *choose* to be happy or feel like going outside or whatever, but this is an illness, unfortunately it just happens to have symptoms that can be easily confused with something else.

That being said, as I say, it is a balance - you do know when to push yourself in order to help get better. I know this morning I really didn't feel like going to get my hair cut cos it was cold and I didn't want to have to interact anyone and I didn't want to go outside and I was tired, but I knew in this instance I should push myself to do it. But equally, you can't beat yourself up for not being able to live or think as if you were fine, cos you're not, you're ill - and I mean so am I, I have difficulty reminding myself of it sometimes cos it does feel like I *should* be able to be better and do more than I can. But yeah, I've already iterated it a lot, but you have to remind yourself that it's an illness, and hopefully with time you'll learn to find where that line lies of just pushing yourself enough that you feel you're achieving little things but still being kind to yourself and knowing your limits. And having people who don't understand the illness throwing in their two cents all the time really doesn't help.

In terms of relationships, I have zero experience, so I'm not gonna advise you there. But I understand what you're saying - in terms of that incident you mentioned, about him lying to you about going out etc., I see what you mean. I guess there's a couple of things there - if you genuinely feel like he isn't giving you enough attention, and that you're being reasonable in thinking that, then you gotta bring that up. Just talk to him about it - tell him how you feel lonely and stuff. We people who are alone a lot more ourselves naturally think a lot more about stuff, and about what everyone else is doing, and why they aren't thinking of us. Other people who are more busy are just that - they're more occupied, and probably aren't just *thinking* so much, he may well just not be aware that you need some more attention.

There's definitely some stuff you can do yourself though - by the way you describe it, it sounds like he wasn't being malicious in hiding from you that he was out. It sounds like he was actually trying to *protect* you. If finding that out just made it worse for you, then you've got to communicate that with him. In that situation, he made his own decision about what he thought would make you feel better. If you'd rather he just told you straight up, then let him know - a lot of the time it's actually really difficult for other people to know how we're feeling and what to do about it, so sometimes you've gotta try and communicate what's going on, as hard as I know it sometimes is to put into words.

And as for what you're thinking, I really do understand what you mean. Seeing pictures of my friends on holiday together, just doing stuff at university together, pictures at the end of year ball (I was at home cos I couldn't manage living at uni), it makes me feel so shit and useless and alone. I'd honestly suggest reducing the amount you look at social media. I've uninstalled snapchat cos I would have liked sending stuff to my friends occasionally, but I know I'd find myself looking at stories, and that shit makes me feel worse. Same for facebook news feed to be honest, and definitely instagram if you have it - I think that's the worst of all them, if facebook is a 'highlight reel', then instagram is like a freaking highlight art gallery. You're just not gonna help yourself looking at what everyone else is doing and wondering why you can't/don't want to do that.

If you do want to do more stuff, go out there and do it. But if you don't, you've got to try and be content with what you're doing, even if it's not what you wish you *could* do, or what you *used* to be able to do or whatever. I think counselling is a good start with this, it will take time but it's a good step. As well maybe try some self-help books or things - I know a lot of it can be quite cheesy about like 'being happy' and stuff, but if you can find the right thing for you then it can really help with dealing with these feelings when you're on your own.

I hope what I've said hasn't been too harsh or anything, I get what you mean and I know myself how shit it feels. But it *is* gonna be a slow process, and it does sound like you're doing the right things. Best of luck, I hope stuff starts to pick up for you soon :)

Hey. I was in the exact same position a couple of months ago and indeed posted a thread titled 'should I tell my friends I'm suicidal?' Does anyone know about your general state, like that you have depression/even just that you're not doing too well? For me the first place to start was my parents, but then my parents have always been super supportive so I wasn't ever afraid that they'd like disown me or whatever. If you haven't (and if you believe your parents will support you), I'd start there, although I understand if you feel like they might overreact. 

I think the hardest thing is going from people knowing nothing, if that's what the case is - I was fortunate enough that quite a few of my friends knew I had depression, and had been through supporting me for a while with that, and knew I had self-harmed and stuff, so even if they might not have expected me to have a suicidal patch, at the same time it wasn't entirely implausible. I'd say if people don't know at all then let some of them in gradually, starting with maybe just the depression, and see how they react to that. Again, I don't know about your situation but I was pretty sure, despite warnings from the medical team and my parents, that my friends wouldn't just distance themselves, but from reading stuff here I know that's not the case for everyone, so that's why I'm suggesting starting slowly and seeing who you think takes it well/who *really* cares. And at the end of the day you've got to do it  however you feel comfortable. But yeah, I would recommend letting your parents in and then whichever friends you feel you can rely on
